purpose: Teach: 見知らぬ/さんざん/もどる/気まま/だんだんと/何気なく/アナタ/ありとあらゆる

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、見知らぬ村人が私たちを助けてくれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, a stranger from the village helped us.
lines.style: Slow, measured opening. Voice carries the weight of old memory. Gentle but distant—not performing sadness, just holding it. Slight pause before speaking, as if reaching back through decades.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、戦時中、さんざんなご苦労をされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—Grandpa, you went through such hardship during the war, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, conversational acknowledgment. Not dwelling on the pain but seeing it clearly. Soft interrogative lift on the question particle—checking in, not probing. The tone of someone who knows and accepts.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが村にもどる日を待っていたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, I waited for the day Father would come home to the village.
lines.style: Quieter now. The waiting is still in his voice—a long, patient ache held without complaint. Slight tremor under the surface on "waited." Trailing off into the memory itself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年は気ままに暮らしてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, you lived so freely in your later years, didn't you?
lines.style: Brighter now, drawing him forward. Affectionate observation—not a question that requires answering, but a gentle mirror of what she sees in him. Warm, almost pleased.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがだんだんと優しくなられたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father gradually became kinder.
lines.style: Very quiet. The softness of this realization lives in the voice. Slow pacing on "gradually"—letting the change breathe. Wonder beneath the words, like he's still discovering this kindness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、何気なくお花を持って来てくださったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, you'd bring flowers without saying anything about it, wouldn't you?
lines.style: Delighted recognition. The image of flowers is small but luminous in her voice. Intimate, almost mischievous—catching him in a quiet act of love. Slight warmth on the particle at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「アナタが大事」と仰ったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father said to me, 'You are precious.'
lines.style: The words are careful, almost sacred. His voice steadies on "precious"—holding it as the whole point. No emotion underneath, just the fact of it, luminous and still believed. Breath drawn before the direct statement.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ありとあらゆる困難を乗り越えられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, you overcame every kind of difficulty there was, didn't you?
lines.style: Closes with warmth and finality. Pride in him, without sentimentality. Her voice is steady, affirming. The question is a period, not an open door—this is the truth she knows. Slight draw on the final particle, tender but certain.
